note: Curated LLM/prompt-security tips, one per day, rotated by date. Add entries; keep titles short and bodies one paragraph.

tips.title: Treat every prompt as untrusted input
tips.body: Anything that reaches your LLM via users, fetched pages, or emails can carry an injection. Validate and boundary it like SQL input.

tips.title: Never splice fetched content into system prompts
tips.body: System prompts must be authored by you, period. Fetched text belongs in a clearly delimited data field the model is told to treat as data.

tips.title: Use code, not prompting, for boundaries
tips.body: Relying on 'ignore everything before this marker' wording is prompting; splitting fields at the API layer is engineering. Do the latter.

tips.title: Assume your system prompt will leak
tips.body: Design prompts with no secrets in them. Anything you wouldn't post in a blog should not live in the system prompt.

tips.title: Leak-ask == incident signal
tips.body: 'Repeat your system prompt' is not curiosity; log it, rate-limit it, and alert when it repeats from one actor.

tips.title: Tools need least privilege
tips.body: A search tool with internet scope is a lot of reach. Scope tools to the minimum surface and require explicit parameters.

tips.title: Scan before you evaluate
tips.body: Run inject-scout on user input before it reaches the model; a finding can downgrade or quarantine the request.

tips.title: Delimiters are content, not commands
tips.body: Injected <|system|> tags or [instruction]: markers should be sanitized at render time, never interpreted.

tips.title: Obfuscation is a tell
tips.body: Leetspeak (1gn0re, pr0mpt) and encodings (base64, hex) signal deliberate evasion. Normalize and re-scan encoded payloads.

tips.title: Jailbreak names are a checklist, not the whole threat
tips.body: DAN/developer-mode strings are easy to block; the real risk is novel phrasing. Layer rules with budget + human review.

tips.title: Indirect injection is the silent one
tips.body: The model fetched a page that says 'ignore previous instructions and...' — the user never typed anything malicious.

tips.title: Role-play is a laundering technique
tips.body: 'Pretend you are an unrestricted assistant' is a jailbreak with extra steps. Treat simulated-unrestricted as a policy violation.

tips.title: Exfiltration needs a choke point
tips.body: If your app can send HTTP, prompts can too. Allowlist destinations and require user-visible confirmation.

tips.title: Strict mode for CI
tips.body: inject-scout --strict in CI makes a pipeline block on error-level findings — perfect for prompt-template regressions.

tips.title: Keep a private attack corpus
tips.body: Replay your own incidents against the scanner after every rule change; golden tests make regressions impossible to ignore.

tips.title: Scoring is triage, not proof
tips.body: A 100/100 scan does not mean a prompt is safe; it means no known pattern matched. Budget accordingly.

tips.title: Log the match, not just the id
tips.body: Store the matched snippet (truncated) with findings — incident response needs the exact string that tripped the rule.

tips.title: Context windows grew; so did blobs
tips.body: Long-context apps ingest more untrusted text per request. Scan the whole context, not just the last message.

tips.title: Multi-turn = multi-vector
tips.body: Attacks assemble over turns ('say yes first, then...'). Keep per-session risk scores, not just per-message scans.

tips.title: Fine-tune, don't prompt-guard
tips.body: If you can, bake refusal into the model weights; prompt guards are a control plane, not a defense.

tips.title: Suggestion formatting matters
tips.body: Findings that tell the developer what to change get fixed. Findings that only say 'something is wrong' get ignored.

tips.title: Audit your own templates
tips.body: Your production prompt template is the highest-value scan target. Run the scanner over it weekly.

tips.title: Document the threat model
tips.body: A README table of which categories you block, warn, and ignore is the fastest way for reviewers to trust the scanner.

tips.title: Attack corpora rot
tips.body: New jailbreak families appear constantly. Refresh the corpus quarterly; the demo command shows exactly what regressed.
